title: Video store midnight
blurb: Thirty-two from the back of the horror aisle, 1981 to 1994. Haunted toymakers, melting winos, a talking brain parasite and a robot dinosaur with a teenager's brain.

films.note: Stranded travelers spend a stormy night with two old toymakers. A mean little fairy tale.
Teens raise the dead on Halloween night. A TV movie with a monster-party streak.
A boy meets the ghost of a murdered girl. Autumn atmosphere, darker than it looks.
A lonely boy, a teddy bear that talks back, and something hungry in the woods.
Kids trade gross-out campfire stories. Anthology nostalgia.
After-hours teens versus the mall's security robots.
An all-night horror marathon with old-school gimmicks, and a killer in the theater.
A boy starts to wonder what's in the family dinners. Suburban black comedy.
Toothy things from space take over a house. Big monster effects on no budget.
A seaside town with an odd relationship to its dead. Go in knowing nothing.
A sick girl's drawings turn into a dream world that won't stay friendly.
A doctor's anatomical dummy becomes part of the family. Quietly disturbing.
An Australian retirement home and a slow-burning gothic dread.
A friendly parasite offers a fantastic high. It wants brains in return.
A young man checks into a grimy New York hotel with something alive in his basket.
A would-be scientist rebuilds his girlfriend. Frankenstein as outrageous comedy.
A rich kid suspects his family's social circle is very wrong. Avoid spoilers.
A machine opens a door to something hungry. Gooey Lovecraft.
Cheap liquor that melts whoever drinks it. Abrasive, and the effects are spectacular.
A health supplement trial goes very wrong in an Australian suburb.
A dead cop investigates his own murder. Buddy-cop action with monster makeup.
The country falls for a dessert that eats back. Consumer satire.
Flesh-eating slugs invade a town. Nastier than it sounds.
A scientist's secret experiment leaves a tentacled surprise at home.
Troubled teens at a wilderness camp, giant bloodsuckers, lots of slime.
A supermarket's night shift meets a killer. Inventive camera, brutal effects.
A theater troupe locked in with an owl-masked killer. Stylish Italian slasher.
A movie theater turns into a demon siege. Heavy-metal excess.
Two brothers run a restaurant with an occult menu. Proudly tasteless.
A mansion stuffed with creatures. Come for the monsters, not the story.
A teenager's brain ends up in a robot dinosaur. Exactly as advertised.
Park rangers versus stop-motion monsters. Handmade midnight madness.
